Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

end verb

come to an end

also come to an end, be over, be finished, finish

classical

Sen. Ep. 24.26: aestās in autumnum dēsinit
Sall. J. 83.2: omne bellum sūmī facile, cēterum aegerrumē dēsinere (Lewis & Short)

dēsinō, dēsinere, dēsiī, dēsitum

verb, third conjugation

end, come to an end

Of things coming to an end; Lewis & Short find this use “not frequent till after the Augustan period”, though Sallust and Ovid have it (dēsierant imbrēs, Ov. Met. 5.285). The same verb as stop (cease).

Other words

  • fīnem habēre — come to an end, have an end

    also used · classical · Ov. F. 5.602: tepidī fīnem tempora vēris habent

  • exeō, exīre, exiī, exitum — run out, end (of a period of time)

    verb, irregular (ex + eō) · also used · classical · Cic. Div. 1.53: quīntō annō exeunte (Lewis & Short); Liv. 4.30.14: indūtiārum diēs exierat (Lewis & Short)

    Of time running out: a year, a truce, the holidays; hieme exeunte, at the end of winter.

Examples

  • diem nox premit, diēs noctem, aestās in autumnum dēsinit, autumnō hiemps īnstat, quae vēre compescitur; omnia sīc trānseunt ut revertantur

    night presses on day and day on night; summer ends in autumn, winter follows hard on autumn and is checked by spring; everything passes only to come backSen. Ep. 24.26

  • nihil est aut certē exiguum est; dūrēmus; jam dēsinet

    It’s nothing, or very little anyway; let’s hold on; it will soon be overSen. Ep. 78.13

  • tum mihi nōn dubiīs auctōribus incipit aestās, et tepidī fīnem tempora vēris habent

    then, on good authority, summer begins for me, and the season of warm spring comes to an endOv. F. 5.601–602

See also end, end, stop, at the end of winter, begin.

SourcesLewis & Short: desino · Lewis & Short: finis · Lewis & Short: exeo
